newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah steady amid ample liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah steady amid ample liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was steady against the dollar in slow early trading on Tuesday.
Dealers said there was no drive in the market to trade, with operators seen mainly extending their forward positions while unloading some long dollar exposures.
But offshore dollar selling was supported by local purchases due to ample domestic liquidity, they said, adding that they still kept watching out for possible post-election unrest.
"There is no initiative to create fresh positions. We see mainly roll-over trades," one major local bank dealer said.
He said offshore operators appeared to extend long forward positions on fears that the central bank might follow measures taken by the Thai central bank to stop quoting tom/next swaps.
Bank Indonesia officials had denied any such plans.
The dealer said, however, offshore players were seen holding on to some long forward positions despite suffering some losses on the recent cheap short-term swap rates.
"They seem to take on such a calculated cost rather then being squeezed unexpectedly," he added.
Spot rupiah was at 2,429.5/30.0 at 0245 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,429.0/30.0.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,429.5/30.15 and 2,429.8/30.25 respectively.
Dealers said election issues were still hanging over the market as the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) will decide on June 5 on whether to accept the election outcome.
PPP had alleged widespread election irregularities.

The ruling Golkar swept more than 74 percent of the votes counted, with the PPP taking nearly 23 percent. Operators were worried of fresh violence and the implications on the rupiah if the PPP declined to accept the election results.
Liquidity was ample, with overnight money traded at around nine percent in the morning. Overnight swaps recovered slightly from a discount in the past few days to 0.05/0.10.
Tom/next swaps edged up to par/0.1 from -0.2/0.1 points.
One-month swaps were at 11.5/13.5, two at 24.0/25.0, three at 35.5/36.5 and six at 72.25/74.00 points.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,417/2,609 and its conversion band also by one point to 2,417/2,465 on Monday.
